Julie Eaton Ernst is a licensed professional civil engineer who specializes in resilient design practices and navigating the intersection of policy and engineered solutions [1]. She is devoted to transforming built, natural, and social environments to be resilient, sustainable, healthy, and equitable [1]. Throughout her career, she has led several award-winning projects that have set the standard for integrating climate projections in the A/E/C industry [1]. She holds bachelor’s degrees in Political Science from the University of Rochester and Civil Engineering from UMass Lowell, and she earned a master’s degree in Civil Engineering from UMass Lowell [1].
